div.head: Northu 2
div.ab: And Godes forboda we forbeodað, þæt ænig preost oðre cirican naðer ne gebicgæ ne geþicgæ, buton hine hwa mid heafodgilte forwyrce, þæt he weofodþenunge þanon forð wyrðe ne sy.
And Godes forbode, we forbeodað þæt ænig preost oðres cirican naðer ne gebicgæ ne geþicgæ, buton hine hwa mid heafodgilte forwyrce þæt he weofodþenunge þanon forð wyrðe ne sy.

Und kraft Gottes Verbot verbieten wir, dass irgend ein Priester eine[s?] andere[n] Kirche weder kaufe noch annehme, ausser wenn jener [andere Pfarrer] durch Capitalverbrechen sich schuldig macht, so dass er hinfort Altardienstes unwürdig sei.

And by God's prohibition we forbid that any priest should either buy or accept another's church, unless that [other priest] has forfeited himself by a capital crime, so that he is henceforth unworthy of altar-service.

And by virtue of God's prohibition we forbid that any priest shall either buy or receive another's church, unless anyone becomes guilty of a capital crime so that he is henceforth unworthy to minister at the altar.

And because of God’s prohibition, we forbid that any priest either buy or accept another’s church, unless the other ruins himself with a capital crime so that afterward he is unworthy to serve at the altar.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

‘oðre’ stands so in D; Thorpe conjectured ‘oðres’ (compare 2.2). D reads ‘gebicgæn’, ‘geþicgæn’ with a dot under the n. Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘And by virtue of God's prohibition, we forbid that any priest shall either buy or sell another's church, unless anyone becomes guilty of a capital crime so that he is henceforth unworthy to minister at the altar.’).
gebicgæ ne geþicgæ: gebicgæn ne geþicgæn with the final n in
